definitions.explanation: A place in a body of water where the depth is shallow, such as a sandbar in the sea or a shallow stretch of a river that can be waded across.

examples.japanese: {船|ふね}が{浅瀬|あさせ}に{乗|の}り{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The boat ran aground on a shoal.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{浅瀬|あさせ}を{歩|ある}いて{渡|わた}ることができる。
examples.english: You can walk across the river at the shallows.

notes:
USAGE:
{浅瀬|あさせ} can refer to shallow areas in rivers, lakes, or the sea. It appears in the proverb {浅瀬|あさせ}に{仇波|あだなみ} (much ado about nothing — literally "waves in the shallows"), describing people who make a fuss over trivial matters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {浅瀬|あさせ}に{乗|の}り{上|あ}げる (to run aground on a shoal)
- {浅瀬|あさせ}を{渡|わた}る (to wade across the shallows)
- {浅瀬|あさせ}で{遊|あそ}ぶ (to play in the shallows)
